facts: 계정당 최대 20개, 파일당 50 MiB. 1 MiB는 1,048,576바이트. failed와 done은 한도 제외, retry_wait는 포함. 등록 전 거절은 시도 아님.
실행기 최대 2개. 등록 시간, 같으면 등록 번호 순서.
30초 무응답 또는 503만 자동 재시도, 201만 성공. 나머지 코드는 실패. 최초 포함 최대 3회, 대기는 2초와 6초.
재시도 대기는 실행기를 점유하지 않고 원래 순서를 유지한다. 대기 종료는 즉시 전송 보장이 아니다.
upload_key는 자동 재시도 동안 유지. 서버는 24시간 결과 보관, 중복 요청에는 같은 파일 번호와 201 반환.
취소는 자동 재시도를 멈추지만 서버 파일을 삭제하지 않는다. 메모리 대기열은 새로 고침 시 사라지고 재등록은 새 키라 중복 방지 미보장.

audience: Junior engineers maintaining a fictional search refresh worker
editing_request: Edit for clarity, natural wording, and suitable pacing while preserving meaning, voice, uncertainty, and concrete details. The facts list is explicitly non-exhaustive; preserve all meaningful information in the source, not only listed facts. Do not invent facts.
facts: Alder uses a document store as the source of truth and a separately refreshed search index.
The worker runs every five minutes, building a separate generation from a snapshot of published documents.
snapshot_at records snapshot time, not build completion time.
Checks require that the generation opens, all indexed documents have IDs, and document count changes by no more than 15%; larger differences require human review.
A failed check preserves the active pointer; passing checks permit an atomic pointer change. Existing requests may finish using the old generation.
After a refresh failure, the active generation is eligible only when its age at request start is at most 20 minutes, calculated using the server clock.
Exactly 20 minutes is eligible; 20 minutes and one second is ineligible. A slow successful build does not reset snapshot age.
Eligible fallback results have stale: true and the specified notice. An empty list is a valid result and must not trigger a different-generation retry.
An absent or over-age active generation returns HTTP 503, the specified error code, and no result items.
No unrestricted database-query fallback is provided because permissions and load would differ.

Tests use a fixed clock for the age boundary and verify failed count checks preserve the pointer. Generation age and failed-refresh count are separate metrics; retries never extend an existing snapshot deadline.

audience: Non-specialist product leads deciding which label to test next
editing_request: Edit for clarity, natural wording, and suitable pacing while preserving meaning, voice, uncertainty, and concrete details. The facts list is explicitly non-exhaustive; preserve all meaningful information in the source, not only listed facts. Do not invent facts.
facts: The Cedar prototype compares Save draft (A) with Save for later (B) for retaining an unfinished request; Submit request sends it to an approver.
The screen otherwise stayed identical and the prototype sent no real requests.
Twelve participants attended moderated English desktop sessions on 14 and 15 September 2026. All arranged shifts monthly or more often; none had used Cedar.
Six saw each version first; all completed a task in each version with different names and dates. Balanced order does not eliminate learning effects.
On first exposure five of six Version B participants and three of six Version A participants chose the intended action without prompting.
Across exposures nine explained no approver notification in B and seven in A; one participant clicked correctly in both but still expected a manager alert.
Four associated draft with email; three found draft technical or uncommon in scheduling. Two asked whether Save for later would automatically submit later.
Recommend Save for later in the next prototype with the specified confirmation sentence and retain Submit request. This is not release approval and adds no automatic submission.
A second round with eight new participants should explicitly check the automatic-submission misunderstanding before a 6 October 2026 release review.
Translations, mobile, screen readers, and real deadline pressure were not tested; the study does not prove overall usability improvement.
